title: Faith in God Elisha
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child describes 2 Kings 6:1-7: the prophets go to the Jordan to cut poles, a borrowed axe head falls into the water, Elisha throws in a stick and the iron floats, and the man lifts it out; God cares even about small needs, so trust him in challenges.

floor.prerequisite: Knows God rescued Peter from prison.
floor.question: How did Peter get out of prison?

representations: a river with an axe head floating
a list of small and big needs
steps: The prophets cut poles at the Jordan.
A borrowed axe head falls into the water.
The iron floats and is lifted out.
contexts: a learner who loses borrowed money

board.do: Draw a river with an axe head under the water.

board.say: Why was the man so upset?

board.do: Wait for the child to say it was borrowed.
Draw the iron floating and write 2 Kings 6:6.

listen_for: Elisha dived in and found it
misconceptions.ask: How was the axe head recovered (2 Kings 6:6)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 2 Kings 6:6: Elisha threw a stick and the iron floated. Iron sinks; only God could make it float.

misconceptions.ask: Whose axe head fell into the water (2 Kings 6:5)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 6:5: "It was borrowed!" The worry was a poor prophet's debt.

listen_for: God cares only about big problems
misconceptions.ask: What does the story teach about small problems?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: why did the man cry out? A borrowed axe was a big worry for him. God cared.

misconceptions.ask: Where were the prophets cutting trees when the axe head fell (2 Kings 6:2-4)?
misconceptions.repair: Read 6:2 and 6:4: they went to the Jordan. Mark it on a map.

checks.question: How was the axe head recovered?
checks.answer: Elisha threw in a stick and the iron floated

checks.question: What does the story teach about small problems?
checks.answer: We can take even small needs to God
